title: Weil equivariance of the completed coefficient duality
statement:
Use the finite-field and coefficient conventions of [def-fix-six-functor-datum]: $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$, and a finite coefficient field $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside the fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, and let $g_X$ be its geometric-Frobenius automorphism. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, use the bounded constructible pro-etale coefficient categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:Lg_X^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$ of [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Put $\omega_{X,\Lambda}=Ra_X^!\Lambda$ and $D_{X,\Lambda}=R\mathcal Hom_\Lambda(-,\omega_{X,\Lambda})$, using the constructible exceptional adjoint and coefficient-passage operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Duality sends Weil complexes contravariantly to Weil complexes. Its evaluation $K\otimes^L_\Lambda D_{X,\Lambda}K\to\omega_{X,\Lambda}$ and canonical biduality isomorphism $\delta_K:K\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,\Lambda}D_{X,\Lambda}K$ are Weil equivariant. For every separated finite-type $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ between separated finite-type $k_0$-schemes, the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ on the geometric fibers lifts to Weil pairs, with equivariant unit and counit. For each finite coefficient-field extension $E\subset L\subset\Qlb$, the canonical dualizing and duality comparisons
$$
\omega_{X,E}\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{X,L},\qquad
(D_{X,E}K)\otimes_E L\xrightarrow{\sim}D_{X,L}(K\otimes_E L)
$$
are Weil equivariant, as are their evaluation, biduality and exceptional-adjunction compatibility diagrams; their images in the common-stage $\Qlb$ category have the same property. These assertions use the rational Frobenius isomorphism itself and require no Frobenius-stable integral lattice.

proof.text: Using the extracted records and fiber instances of [def-coef-verdier-weil-data], apply [lem-coef-weil-normalized-duality] to obtain B_X with its internal-Hom and dualizing identifications and a normalized Weil structure W_X. For each relative morphism use [lem-coef-weil-left-exchange-compatibility] to choose B_Y with its normalized Weil structure W_Y and A with their relative exceptional formula and normalized left exchanges. Apply [lem-coef-weil-exceptional-compatibility] to the chosen left exchanges. The resulting witnesses give exactly Conclusion.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X_0$ be a scheme over $\mathbf F_q$ with geometric fiber $X$, and let
$\Lambda\in\{E,\Qlb\}$, regarded as a condensed ring. Duality
$\mathbb D_X=R\mathcal Hom(-,\omega_X)$ on $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ carries Weil
complexes $(K,\theta_K)$ in the sense of [sk-def-sf-weil-complexes] to Weil
complexes. Evaluation, biduality, the exceptional adjunction data, and the
comparisons under finite extension of the coefficient field are Weil
equivariant. This does not require a Frobenius-stable integral lattice for a
rational Weil complex.

proof.text:
The underlying operations preserve $\Dbc(X,\Lambda)$ and biduality holds
there for every admissible $\Lambda$ ([sk-thm-sf-ctf-stability],
[sk-thm-existence], [sk-thm-pd-verdier-duality]). Consequently the equivariance construction of
[lem-fix-weil-operations] applies, including to the
dualizing object supplied by the exceptional adjoint. Write
$g$ for geometric Frobenius and
$\theta_K:g^*K\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ for a Weil structure as in
[def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. The dual Weil structure is
the composite

$$
g^*\mathbb DK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb D(g^*K)
\xrightarrow{\mathbb D(\theta_K^{-1})}\mathbb DK.
$$

The first map is the internal-Hom comparison for the equivalence
$g^*$ of $D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$, using the dualizing Weil
structure. Naturality of evaluation proves its equivariance, and
transposition gives the same conclusion for $\delta$. All of this takes
place in $D(X_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$ with $\theta_K$ itself; no
integral lattice and no finite coefficient field is needed. (If one wishes
to work over a finite field of coefficients when $\Lambda=\Qlb$,
[sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] descends $K$, $\theta_K$ and its inverse to
one finite $E'$, as a consequence.)

The comparisons of [lem-coef-integral-finite-extension] and
[sk-prop-scalar-six] for extension of scalars are built from scalar tensor,
the dualizing counit, and evaluation, and $g^*$ commutes with extension of
scalars, so they commute with the displayed dual Weil structures. The same
units and counits as in [lem-fix-weil-operations] give the
exceptional-adjunction assertion.
